summary: Topical compilation of Kirpal Singh's letters, circulars and talks. Book Three (Meditation) is the most systematic statement of his light practice: sit in any posture that can be held longest without moving, stay wide awake, direct attention to the seat of the soul behind and between the eyebrows, and look 'sweetly and serenely' into the middle of the darkness in front, repeating the five charged names slowly and at intervals; the gaze is constant, the repetition intermittent. No strain on eyes or forehead, no attention to breath or body. Chapters on difficulties, 'inaccuracies', dangers and dry spells diagnose why nothing is seen (clutching, strain, divided attention, lapses recorded in the diary) and tell the disciple that the inner Master grants experience 'at the opportune moment'. Also covers looking into the middle of whatever light appears so that it 'bursts', and the radiant form.
why_relevant: Step-by-step instruction plus dedicated troubleshooting chapters for a practice whose stated first result is seen inner light; addresses the person who sees only darkness.
